findings.title: NPE when the "Clients" resource-type resource does not exist
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no per-client resource exists the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, which can legitimately return `null` (it returns null when the realm's `adminPermissionsEnabled` flag is off, or when the `Clients` resource simply does not exist in the resource server, e.g. a realm whose admin-permissions client was initialized before the `Clients` resource type was added). The returned value is immediately passed to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later to `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)` without a null check, producing a NullPointerException / HTTP 500 on ordinary admin endpoints such as GET/PUT /clients/{id}. A null check returning `false` is needed.

findings.title: No upgrade path for realms whose admin-permissions client was already initialized
findings.body: `init()` creates the authorization scopes and the per-resource-type "all" resources only once, when the admin permissions client is first created (it returns early if `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`). Realms that already enabled ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 before this change therefore have neither the new `Clients` resource nor the new scopes `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`. For those realms, creating a Clients permission fails (`getOrCreateResource` throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` when a scope is missing) and client permission evaluation hits the missing `Clients` resource. Either a migration that adds missing scopes/resources, or lazy creation on demand, is required.

findings.title: Client/role/group removal breaks when both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and V2 are enabled
findings.body: The removal listener is now guarded by `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`, but `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. With both features enabled (they are independent flags), a `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` now calls `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` -> `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. The event listener runs inside the removal transaction, so deleting a client fails with a server error instead of cleaning up V1 permission policies. The listener should select the V1 management implementation explicitly (or the V2 implementation must tolerate these calls).

findings.title: Overridden methods throwing UnsupportedOperationException turn 403/legacy paths into 500s
findings.body: `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource` and the `*Permission(ClientModel)` methods all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. These are still reached at runtime when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled: the token-exchange flow calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...)` to decide whether an exchange to another client is allowed, and the `/clients/{id}/management/permissions` admin endpoints call `isPermissionsEnabled`/`setPermissionsEnabled` (the latter only requires the V1 feature, which can be enabled simultaneously). The result is an HTTP 500 instead of the previous Forbidden/clean response. These methods should return a safe value (e.g. `false`) or the call sites must be guarded.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the resource-type resource name and misses per-client resources
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` and collects `resource.getName()`. Two problems: (1) the "all clients" resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` has both name and type equal to `Clients`, so when an all-clients permission is granted the literal string `"Clients"` is added to the returned set and is then treated by callers as a client id; (2) per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` are created without a type (`setType` is never called), so `findByType` never returns them and clients that have individual permissions are not reported. The method therefore returns wrong data for callers that filter client listings by granted permission.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for the Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` only resolves human-readable names for the `Users` resource type. For the newly added `Clients` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (only name=clientId-UUID and owner are set). Consequently the admin REST/console representation of a client permission shows a null/empty resource name instead of the client's clientId, and there is no "All clients" label analogous to "All users".

findings.title: Javadoc on require* methods documents a return value for void methods
findings.body: `requireView()` (line 95-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100-103) are documented as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}" / "...if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but both methods are `void` and throw ForbiddenException when the check fails, like the other `require*` methods in this interface. The docs should state the throwing behaviour, otherwise implementers/callers are misled about the contract.

findings.title: New map-roles-client-scope scope and client-scope permissions are untested
findings.body: The PR adds the scopes `configure`, `map-roles`, `map-roles-composite`, `map-roles-client-scope` and the client-scope related evaluations (`canManage(ClientScopeModel)`, `canView(ClientScopeModel)`, `canManageClientScopes()`), but the new tests only cover MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. `canMapClientScopeRoles` / `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and the ClientScopeModel-based checks have no coverage, so regressions in those code paths (including the ones that intentionally differ from V1) would go unnoticed.
